      "unit": "F000",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Section 717 of title 38, United States Code, as added by subsection (a)(1), shall apply with respect to any 365-day period beginning on or after the date of enactment of Pub. L. 114–315 (December 16, 2016).",

        "actor_quote": null,
        "kind": "statement",

    {
      "unit": "F004:F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": [
          "t_covered_service_719"
        ],
        "statement": "The Secretary shall order that the covered service of an employee of the Department removed from a position for performance or misconduct under section 713, 714, or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law shall not be taken into account for purposes of calculating an annuity with respect to such individual under chapter 83 or chapter 84 of title 5, if the Secretary determines that the individual is convicted of a felony (and the conviction is final) that influenced the individual's performance while employed in the position; before such order is made, the individual is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond to the proposed order by not later than ten business days following receipt of such notice; and the Secretary issues the order not later than five business days after receiving the response of the individual (in the case of a proposed order to which an individual responds under subparagraph (B)(ii)) or not later than 15 business days after providing notice under subparagraph (B)(i) (in the case of a proposed order to which an individual does not respond).",
        "actor": "The Secretary",
        "actor_quote": "The Secretary",
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": "When an employee of the Department is removed from a position for performance or misconduct under section 713, 714, or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law, and the statutory conviction, notice, and timing conditions are satisfied",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F004:F011"
        ],
        "context_quotes": null,
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "choice_text": null,
        "choice_quote": null,
        "alternative_quotes": null,
        "logic_quote": null,
        "references": [
          "section 713",

          "section 7461",

        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Any individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under 38 U.S.C. § 719(a) may appeal the reduction to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management pursuant to such regulations as the Director may prescribe for purposes of that subsection.",
        "actor": "Any individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under this subsection",
        "actor_quote": "Any individual with respect to whom an annuity is reduced under this subsection",
        "kind": "permission",
        "modality": "may",
        "scope_text": "With respect to an individual whose annuity is reduced under 38 U.S.C. § 719(a)",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F013"
        ],
        "context_quotes": null,
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "choice_text": null,
        "choice_quote": null,
        "alternative_quotes": null,

    {
      "unit": "F016:F023",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": [
          "t_covered_service_719"
        ],
        "statement": "The Secretary may order that the covered service of an individual who the Secretary proposes to remove for performance or misconduct under section 713, 714, or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law but who leaves employment at the Department prior to the issuance of a final decision with respect to such action shall not be taken into account for purposes of calculating an annuity with respect to such individual under chapter 83 or chapter 84 of title 5, if the Secretary determines that the individual is convicted of a felony (and the conviction is final) that influenced the individual's performance while employed in the position; before such order is made, the individual is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond to the proposed order by not later than ten business days following receipt of such notice; and the Secretary issues the order not later than five business days after receiving the response of the individual (if the individual responds under subparagraph (B)(ii)) or not later than 15 business days after providing notice under subparagraph (B)(i) (if the individual does not respond).",
        "actor": "The Secretary",
        "actor_quote": "The Secretary",
        "kind": "permission",
        "modality": "may",
        "scope_text": "With respect to an individual whom the Secretary proposes to remove for performance or misconduct under section 713, 714, or 7461 of title 38 or any other provision of law but who leaves employment at the Department prior to the issuance of a final decision with respect to such action, when the specified felony conviction, notice, and timing criteria are satisfied",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F016:F023"

        "context_quotes": null,
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "choice_text": null,

    {

      "unit_attributes": {

        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Upon the issuance of an order by the Secretary under paragraph (1) of 38 U.S.C. § 719(b), the individual shall have an opportunity to appeal the order to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management before the date that is seven business days after the date of such issuance.",
        "actor": "the individual",
        "actor_quote": "the individual",
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": "Upon the issuance of an order by the Secretary under 38 U.S.C. § 719(b)(1)",

      "unit": "F049:F057",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary may issue an order directing an employee of the Department to repay the amount, or a portion of the amount, of any award or bonus paid to the employee under title 5, including under chapters 45 or 53 of such title, or title 38 if the Secretary determines that the individual engaged in misconduct or poor performance prior to payment of the award or bonus, and that such award or bonus would not have been paid, in whole or in part, had the misconduct or poor performance been known prior to payment; before such repayment, the employee is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond to the proposed order by not later than 10 business days after the receipt of such notice; and the Secretary issues the order not later than five business days after receiving the response of the individual (in the case of a proposed order to which an individual responds under paragraph (2)(B)) or not later than 15 business days after providing notice under paragraph (2)(A) (in the case of a proposed order to which an individual does not respond).",

        "actor_quote": "the Secretary",
        "kind": "permission",
        "modality": "may",

      "unit_attributes": {
        "defines_term": null,
        "term_refs": null,
        "statement": "Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary may issue an order directing an employee of the Department to repay the amount, or a portion of the amount, paid to or on behalf of the employee under title 5 for relocation expenses, including any expenses under section 5724 or 5724a of such title, or title 38 if the Secretary determines that relocation expenses were paid following an act of fraud or malfeasance that influenced the authorization of the relocation expenses; before such repayment, the employee is afforded notice of the proposed order and an opportunity to respond to the proposed order not later than ten business days following the receipt of such notice; and the Secretary issues the order not later than five business days after receiving the response of the individual (in the case of a proposed order to which an individual responds under paragraph (2)(B)) or not later than 15 business days after providing notice under paragraph (2)(A) (in the case of a proposed order to which an individual does not respond).",
